key_insight: Under illustrative routing costs, calibration-selected abstention cut logistic regression’s held-out test cost by 38.1% and wrong routes from 15.3% to 3.5%.
engineering_relevance: When misrouting costs more than human triage, evaluate frozen route-or-defer policies by operational cost rather than accuracy or calibration error alone.
method: Compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four LLMs using zero- and few-shot prompts.
Select abstention policies on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate once on held-out test data.
Assess confidence using ECE, correctness AUROC, and tie-aware risk-coverage area.
evidence_signal: On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, TF-IDF logistic regression with a calibration-selected 0.60 threshold reduced test cost from 0.763 to 0.472 under costs (correct, triage, wrong) = (0, 1, 5), with a 95% CI of 35.7%–40.4% for the relative reduction.
watch_item: Results depend on the dataset, prompts, model endpoints, and assumed costs; improved calibration alone does not guarantee useful error discrimination or deployment readiness.
paper_title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
